newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil imports seen rising on short crop.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil imports seen rising on short crop.

text.p: An expected fall in Pakistan's cotton crop, a byproduct of which is cottonseed oil, will drive up edible oil imports next year, analysts say.

"Pakistan will have to import 55,000 tonnes more vegoil to meet the shortfall, mainly due to a short cotton crop," Sattar Balagamwala, vice-chairman of the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association, told Reuters.

He said cotton output was likely to reach 8.6 million 170-kg bales in 1996/97 (July-June), implying cottonseed oil production of about 295,000 tonnes. In 1995/96, Pakistan produced 9.94 million bales of cotton and 350,000 tonnes of cottonseed oil.
"The cottonseed oil gap will be about 55,000 tonnes, which will have to be imported," said Balagamwala.

Vegoil imports slowed to 382,976 tonnes worth $278 million in first five months 1996/97 from 493,391 tonnes worth $406 million in same period of 1995/96, partly because of earlier expectations of a bumper cotton crop of 11 to 12 million bales.
"Vegoil imports are likely to pick up now after downward (cotton crop) estimates by growers," Balagamwala said.

Tanwir Hassan, chairman of the Pakistan Vanaspati Manufacturers Association, said prices of vegetable ghee (edible oil) had risen faster than those of other staple food items between 1991 and 1996, mainly due to higher palm oil prices and repeated devaluations of the rupee against the dollar.
Pakistan's per capita consumption of edible oil was likely to stay at about 12 kg (26 lb). "Therefore total consumption is estimated at 1.676 million tonnes in 1996/97," Hassan said.
Malaysian authorities say Pakistan's vegoil imports are expected to rise sharply by 2000.

Pakistan's oils and fats consumption could climb to 2.65 million tonnes by 2000 from 2.39 million in 1995, compared to 2.07 million in 1991, Mamat Bin Salleh of Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority said in Karachi last week.

Oils and fats production in Pakistan had averaged 0.84 million tonnes a year from 1991 to 1995. "In 1995, Pakistan produced about 374,000 tonnes of cottonseed oil, 66,000 tonnes of rapeseed oil, 30,000 tonnes of sunflower oil, 10,000 tonnes of coconut/soya oil and 380,000 tonnes of butter," Salleh said.
He said it was hard to assess future domestic oilseed production, but it could reach about one million tonnes by 2000.

The growth of vegetable oil imports in Pakistan in recent years is mainly due to expanding demand that could be attributed to population growth, increased urbanisation, increase in per capita income, competitive prices and private sector participation in the import trade, he said.
